Write a query to one Parquet file per partition, sorted

Source: R/species.R
obis_h3_write_partitions.Rd

The explicit per-partition writer of the species table. DuckDB's COPY ... PARTITION_BY wrote thousands of files per resolution for 301 classes and lost the sort order (spike 2), so this materializes sql once, then runs one COPY per partition value to dir/<key>=<value>[/<key2>=<value2>]/data_0.parquet, each ORDER BY order_by with fixed row groups, so a reader finds a cell's rows in one row group from the cell_id statistics. A NULL partition value is written as null_value (_none; DuckDB-WASM reads __HIVE_DEFAULT_PARTITION__ as a string), and other values are percent-encoded where needed (DuckDB decodes them on read). The partition columns are left out of the files (they are in the path).

Usage

obis_h3_write_partitions(
  con,
  sql,
  dir,
  partition_by = "class",
  order_by = c("cell_id", "aphiaid"),
  null_value = "_none",
  compression = "zstd",
  row_group_size = 100000L
)

Arguments

con

a DBI connection to DuckDB.

sql

a SELECT yielding the partition columns and the file columns.

dir

output directory (created).

partition_by

the partition column(s), outermost first (default "class").

order_by

the sort columns within a file (default c("cell_id", "aphiaid")).

null_value

the on-disk value of a NULL partition (default "_none").

compression

Parquet codec (default "zstd").

row_group_size

rows per row group (default 100000; DuckDB rounds up to a multiple of 2048).

Value

a data frame, one row per partition: the partition columns, path (relative to dir) and rows.
